subject: Phase 100260: Retention Mission Policy and Coding-Agent First-Run Defaults
verdict_justification: The adversarial findings were all resolved in remediation round 1: the published profile schema no longer carries any $ref (mission-entry schema is inlined, so it stays valid under any document embedding), a schema_refs_resolve pointer check now runs inside clio-mcp validate_tool_schema so a dangling ref fails the schema-pack tests, secret-bearing mission entries are rejected at validate() time with hygiene-tooling guidance and without echoing the secret, the upgrade-behavior change for pre-existing unconfigured repo: banks is disclosed in the phase file Known Limitations (section 9 and section 12), and all test files carry the AGENTS.md header. The opt-in migration mechanism was not implemented (documented limitation instead; product scope decision). make check exit 0; workspace coverage 97.87% lines / 98.88% functions with 0 files below 90% on either metric.

requirements.requirement: Task 2: Deterministic Mission Influence on Admission
requirements.evidence: Arithmetic utility adjustments (-0.30 drop / +0.15 keep), drop veto with mission_drop reason, gate order preservation, and audit rule IDs are fully implemented and verified in tests.
coding_default_profile implemented with standard 20-line chatter fixture calibrating to 4 admit / 16 drop; wired to new repo: banks at resolution time.

Regex evaluation is timeout-bounded by a 50k step budget, and labels scrub secrets in previews; however, mission examples with secret patterns are not rejected at set time. Remediated r1: RetentionMission::validate rejects secret-bearing entries (scrub_inline_secrets delta) with hygiene guidance; test secret_bearing_entries_are_rejected_with_hygiene_guidance.

Remediated r1: mission-entry schema inlined (no $ref), schema_refs_resolve wired into validate_tool_schema over the whole pack; test validate_flags_unresolvable_ref_pointers covers the defect path.

All 48 files are strictly <= 450 lines (max 443 lines), but four new test files omit the required //! # Responsibility header section. Remediated r1: //! # Responsibility headings added to the four flagged files (plus schema_retention_defs_tests.rs, same class); retention_mission_harness.rs got the full structure.

issues.title: Broken JSON Schema $ref pointer in published profile_json_schema and missing definition in MCP tool schemas
issues.why_it_matters: MCP clients and tooling validating tool calls or config against profile_json_schema fail with PointerToNowhere errors because the $ref points to /properties/mission/x-mission-entry which does not exist. Furthermore, x-mission-entry is missing from the MCP tool schemas.
issues.impact: Any standard JSON Schema validator fails on tool parameter validation for retention_profile_set and admit_preview_batch.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention_schema.rs:105, 112, 123. Running python jsonschema.validate() produces '_WrappedReferencingError PointerToNowhere: /properties/mission/x-mission-entry does not exist'.
issues.proposed_fix: Move x-mission-entry into definitions or under mission.properties, update the $ref paths to point correctly to the definition, and ensure schema_retention_defs embeds the definition.
issues.resolution: Fixed by inlining the mission-entry schema into the keep/drop item schemas (crates/clio-config/src/retention_schema.rs mission_entry_schema()), removing every $ref from the published schema (x-mission-entry root key removed) and adding schema_refs_resolve(), an RFC 6901 pointer checker, wired into clio-mcp validate_tool_schema (crates/clio-mcp/src/schema.rs) so every published tool schema is checked. Evidence: test published_schema_has_no_dangling_refs (clio-config), validate_flags_unresolvable_ref_pointers (clio-mcp), workspace JSON run shows 0 files below 90%.

issues.title: Secret-bearing mission patterns are not rejected at set time and persist unmasked in profile configuration
issues.why_it_matters: Section 7 Security Constraints explicitly requires: 'Never commit secrets; mission examples containing secret patterns are rejected with guidance to use hygiene tooling instead.' Unchecked examples store credentials in plaintext on disk.
issues.impact: Users or tools providing secret patterns in keep/drop examples cause raw API keys or passwords to be persisted in profiles.json.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention_mission.rs:143-215 (RetentionMission::validate). Executing 'am retention set' with an api_key string succeeds and writes the unmasked credential to disk.
issues.proposed_fix: Add secret pattern detection using clio_config::secret to RetentionMission::validate(), returning an InvalidArgument error guiding the user to hygiene tools.
issues.resolution: Fixed: RetentionMission::validate now rejects an entry whose text changes under clio_config::secret::scrub_inline_secrets (key: value / key=value secret shapes), returning InvalidArgument with guidance to scrub with the hygiene tooling (hygiene_audit / hygiene_clean) and without echoing the raw secret. Evidence: test secret_bearing_entries_are_rejected_with_hygiene_guidance in crates/clio-config/src/retention_mission_tests.rs asserts rejection, hygiene guidance, and that the error does not echo the secret; marker words without a value still pass.

issues.title: Pre-existing unconfigured repo: banks automatically switch to coding_default_profile on upgrade without mention in Known Limitations
issues.why_it_matters: Existing banks created before Phase 100260 with repo: prefix that did not set an explicit profile previously had balanced verbosity and no mission; after upgrade they immediately resolve coding default.
issues.impact: Unexpected admission behavior change for pre-existing unconfigured repositories without notice in Known Limitations.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention_store.rs:106-109 applies coding_default_profile to all repo: banks lacking a stored profile. Phase file §9 and §12 Known Limitations do not disclose this upgrade behavior.
issues.proposed_fix: Document in §9 and §12 Known Limitations that pre-existing repo: banks without stored profiles resolve coding_default_profile rather than the builtin default.
issues.resolution: Fixed by documentation: phase file section 9 Known limitations item (e) and section 12 Known Limitations now disclose that pre-existing repo: banks without a stored profile resolve coding_default_profile after this phase, and that no opt-out mechanism ships (store an explicit profile to override). Attribution row updated with the Remediator r1 row.

unknowns.what: Step-budget accounting is now per-position in the iterative repeat_term; worst-case step counts match the recursive form but a full equivalence fuzz over the pinned grammar was not run.
unknowns.why_unknown: Equivalence is established by the existing 13 matcher tests plus the new greedy_repetition_backtracks_to_shorter_counts test (a*ab / a+ab backtracking cases), not by exhaustive fuzzing.
unknowns.what_would_resolve_it: A differential fuzz harness against the recursive reference implementation or the regex crate.
unknowns.materiality: Low (deterministic engine, bounded inputs, 50k step budget).

strengths: Zero-allocation FNV-1a 64 content hashing provides deterministic, stable rule IDs across edits.

All 48 staged files comply with the 450-line file length limit, including refactored schema modules.

Did not add explicit security test cases attempting to set secret tokens in mission examples. (Addressed in remediation.)
